title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: LumApps Agents, Agents Space & MCP
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: Watch the replay of our hands-on tour of the LumApps Agents Hub, where we show you how to build, govern, and connect your own AI agents, from external agent-to-agent integrations to the LumApps MCP in Claude and ChatGPT. It also includes a time-saving styling pro tip and the highlights of LumApps’ biggest release yet.
lead: Watch the replay of our hands-on tour of the LumApps Agents Hub, where we show you how to build, govern, and connect your own AI agents, from external agent-to-agent integrations to the LumApps MCP in Claude and ChatGPT. It also includes a time-saving styling pro tip and the highlights of LumApps’ biggest release yet.
html:
The replay of our October ADC Live! episode is now available, and it may be our most packed session yet. We took a hands-on tour of the LumApps Agents Hub, showed how LumApps connects to external agents and AI assistants through MCP, and walked through the October release note.

We'll say it plainly: we were impressed. In nearly a decade of reading LumApps release notes, this is one of the deepest we have seen. It marks the moment LumApps stops being just a digital workplace and becomes a single entry point to your physical workplace, your digital workplace, and your AI agents.

Here's what we covered, and why it matters for your LumApps platform.


Pro tip: clone a platform style in seconds

If you manage several sites that share one brand, platform styles are the way to keep them consistent. But what if five of your six sites need a small variation, like a different secondary color? Out of the box, that means rebuilding a style by hand: custom code, slideshow headers, palettes, headers and footers. Done carefully, that can take hours.

The LumApps APIs can copy a platform style, but they can't rename the copy. So we built a Platform Style Manager into the ADC Toolbox. Search for any platform style, duplicate it under a new name, then adjust the palette in LumApps. In the episode, we cloned our own brand style and recolored it live in under a minute.


The October release: physical meets digital

The October release note is huge, with updates across search, CMS and more. For us, its biggest story is the first wave of what LumApps announced at its Bright events this spring: the convergence of the physical and digital workplace.

  • Venue access. The new Workplace Experience bundle lets you manage access to your offices and venues directly in LumApps. No separate platform to build, and no extra maintenance for IT.

  • Digital signage. Push messages to frontline employees on screens across your venues, managed from the same platform.

  • One solution, one license. Capabilities that companies often buy separately or build in-house now come with LumApps.

We were also proud to see LumApps feature our own Text-to-Speech Page Reader in the release. Its latest update adds phonetic pronunciation, so names and initiatives are never mispronounced; playback speed control, like voice notes in WhatsApp; and custom widget selection, giving page admins more control and readers a better experience.

You can find the full release notes in the Product section of the LumApps Hive. We'll dig into more of them in upcoming episodes.


Inside the LumApps Agents Hub

We're excited to share that ADC has earned the level-two LumApps Agents Hub certification, the highest of the two partner levels. Level one covers where AI lives across LumApps and how agents are configured. Level two covers building your own agents, grounding them in your workplace knowledge, and connecting LumApps to agents that already exist elsewhere.

In the episode, we walked through a live job-openings agent we built, from the employee's view to the admin's:

  • Agents library. A new icon in the top bar takes any employee to a library of the agents available to them. The feature is in beta and expected to roll out to everyone in the coming weeks; ask LumApps to enable it for you.

  • Chat bubble and Ask AI. Employees can start a conversation from the chat bubble, with conversation starters to get going, or simply search. Ask AI answers at the top of search results and shows which agent responded.

  • Personalized answers. Agents can use the employee's profile, such as department and job title, as context. Our job-openings agent suggests roles that actually fit the person asking.

  • Global and per-agent instructions. Global instructions act as a system prompt for every agent. Each agent adds its own instructions, tone, specialization and conversation starters on top.

  • Knowledge sources. Ground agents in your own content, filtered by site, content type and metadata, or draw from communities, directories, the media library and users.

  • Audience. Decide exactly who can reach each agent, from the whole company to a small group.

That last point is what makes this enterprise-grade. Many organizations are struggling to govern AI agents, and LumApps now builds that governance right into the platform.


Agent-to-agent and MCP: LumApps as your AI front door

This is the part that surprised us most. LumApps doesn't just host its own agents; it connects to the ones you already have.

  • Agent-to-agent (A2A) protocol. Connect external agents that already work across your company, through the A2A protocol or a link, then manage and govern them from LumApps. Without this, many organizations would need a separate agent governance tool such as Workato.

  • The LumApps MCP server. LumApps already exposes a large set of MCP tools, including tools to list agents. That means your LumApps agents can be reached from the AI assistant your people already prefer, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot.

LumApps' documentation focuses on Copilot and similar enterprise tools, but the same setup carries over to other assistants, and it's straightforward. The result is one platform that serves as the entry point to your physical workplace, your digital workplace, and all of your AI agents and tools. That's real bang for your buck.


Where we can help

Creating agents in LumApps is easy enough that your team can start on its own. Where we can make the biggest difference is in the advanced work: bring your own LLM, bring your own components, and connecting your existing corporate tools and agents to LumApps. If that's on your roadmap, let's talk.


Coming up next: LumApps Play

Next month, we're turning to LumApps Play, LumApps' enterprise-grade video solution. Better still, we won't be the only ones talking. A longtime LumApps customer from The Glass Guru will join us to share how they've used LumApps Play in their workplace for over a year. If you already have LumApps Play or are considering it as a new or replacement video platform, you won't want to miss it.


Watch the replay

Catch the full episode now, and tell us what you think. Visit the ADC partner space on the LumApps Hive and use the feedback button at the top. Have a question about anything we covered? Reach out to your LumApps CSM or contact us directly. We'd love to help.

title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: Deep Dive into the LumApps Enterprise Search Experience
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: After a summer break, Misha and Ivo return with a full episode on search. Ivo, a former LumApps search product owner, explains where the search engine came from and where it's likely heading. Misha shows admins how to tune search filters and how LumApps can now find content buried inside uploaded PDFs.
lead: After a summer break, Misha and Ivo return with a full episode on search. Ivo, a former LumApps search product owner, explains where the search engine came from and where it's likely heading. Misha shows admins how to tune search filters and how LumApps can now find content buried inside uploaded PDFs.
html:
Back from summer, straight into search

We took about a month off over the summer. When we came back, we picked the topic people ask us about most: enterprise search.

This one is personal for Ivo. Before ADC, he was the product owner for search at LumApps, so he knows the engine better than almost anyone outside the search team.

Pro tip: you control the search filters

Many global admins don't know this, but you can configure the filters on the LumApps search page. In the back office, go to Search, and you'll see the default configuration. You can create your own from there.

A custom configuration lets you:

  • Choose your sources. LumApps content is the default, and Google Drive and SharePoint are both available natively.

  • Pick result types. Include or exclude contents, posts, users, spaces, communities, directory entries, videos, learning, and more.

  • Edit and reorder filters. Remove ones nobody uses, or move the important ones, like Author, to the top.

Before you add more filters, check your search analytics. Most people type a query, scan the results, and rarely touch the filters. Fewer, better-placed filters usually work better.

Ivo's tip for testing: don't edit your live configuration directly. Build a second one, activate it during off-hours in your time zones, test it, and switch back. As far as we know, you can't limit a test configuration to a specific group yet, so timing is your safety net.

Still excited about: Page Reader

Our Page Reader widget reads any LumApps page aloud, either the whole page or just a selection. It offers around 20 voices and works well for news articles and knowledge content. Because it doesn't use third-party AI, you don't need to go through an AI approval process to roll it out.

A short history of LumApps search

Ivo gave the backstory:

  • 2019: LumApps rebuilt its search engine from scratch. It's more powerful than most people realize, and many of its capabilities have never been released as features.

  • Around 2021: The focus shifted to partners like Coveo, which was the best option at the time for connecting many content sources.

  • The Search SDK era: Customers could plug in any search engine, but it took a developer, and results appeared in a separate tab.

  • Today: AI, agents, and Ask AI are getting the spotlight, and search powers all of them behind the scenes.

The July 9 release notes showed the first signs of change, including semantic search for content admins.

Why native search has to catch up

Ivo used the Kano model from product management to explain the pressure on LumApps. Some features are basic expectations: if every product on the market can open a can and yours can't, customers won't even consider it. With so many search tools on the market, strong native search is now one of those basic expectations.

His predictions:

  • Synonyms will return.

  • Result clustering will arrive, something the team was already discussing in 2019.

  • Native connectors will let results from tools like Salesforce or ServiceNow appear in LumApps without the SDK or an extra tab.

Will a third-party engine come back as the answer? Ivo doesn't think so. Between Ask AI and the LumApps MCP, he expects LumApps to keep investing in its own engine.

Three ways LumApps search finds things

  • Exact match: finds the words you typed, as you typed them.

  • Semantic: looks at what you mean. Someone searching "time off" might really need your HR or expense tool.

  • Fuzzy: handles typos and small spelling variations.

The feature we use every day: searching inside documents

The July release also improved knowledge extraction for media documents, and this is the one Misha was most excited about.

Until now, connected sources like Drive or Box showed results in their own tab, so users had to click around to find files. The goal is one search feed with everything in it, and this update is a real step in that direction.

Upload a PDF to the LumApps media library, and search will index what's inside it, not just the title. In the demo, Misha searched for "Page Reader" and found a PDF bundle whose title had nothing to do with Page Reader. The match came from text inside the file.

There's one important limitation: you can't set visibility on media documents yet. Any file you upload will show up in search for everyone. For now, use this feature for organization-wide content, like benefits guides, general documentation, and design assets, and keep restricted files elsewhere.


Let's take a look at the replay:

title: Interim Release Notes by LumApps Marketplace | Page Reader by ADC
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: We have some news to share: LumApps has featured our Page Reader extension in its latest interim release notes, under LumApps Add-ons on the Marketplace.
lead: We have some news to share: LumApps has featured our Page Reader extension in its latest interim release notes, under LumApps Add-ons on the Marketplace.
html:
For a partner, that's a big deal. Release notes are where LumApps tells admins, comms teams, and IT leaders what's new and worth their attention. Seeing an ADC widget listed there, next to LumApps' own updates, tells us we're building the right things for the people who use the platform every day.

What got featured

Page Reader turns any LumApps page into spoken audio with one click. Employees can listen to news, policies, and knowledge base articles at their desk, on their commute, or wherever they are. It doesn't require a plugin or any setup for end users, and it's natively integrated with LumApps.

The release notes highlight what we think matters most:

  • Choice of voices and languages to fit your brand and your audience

  • Equal access for every employee, regardless of reading ability or screen time

  • Listening anywhere, at a desk or on the move

They also highlight privacy. Page Reader runs entirely in the user's browser, and page content is never sent to a third party. For organizations with sensitive internal content, that's often the deciding factor.

Why this matters to us

ADC has worked in the LumApps ecosystem since 2017. We've built custom widgets, integrations, and analytics for organizations of all sizes. Page Reader came from a question we kept hearing: how do we reach employees who don't have time to read, or who find reading harder than listening?

Being recognized in LumApps' release notes is a nice confirmation that the question was worth answering. Thank you to the LumApps team for the shout-out.

How to get it

Page Reader is available to LumApps customers with a license from ADC and one of the following:

  • Enterprise or Employee Hub

  • Business, Professional, or Social Intranet with the Marketplace, Companion, or Micro-apps add-on

Want to hear it on your own pages? We'll set up a demo or a trial.

Read the documentation | View the LumApps release notes | Contact us

title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: Enterprise Links Module (Directory Entries)
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: Directory entries are one of the oldest modules in LumApps, and they've picked up some new features. Misha and Ivo show how to bulk import links, add custom fields like contact emails and phone numbers, manage permissions, and run micro apps right inside a directory.
lead: Directory entries are one of the oldest modules in LumApps, and they've picked up some new features. Misha and Ivo show how to bulk import links, add custom fields like contact emails and phone numbers, manage permissions, and run micro apps right inside a directory.
html:
Hot weather, older module


Ivo joined us from under a European heat dome. We stayed indoors and talked about directory entries, the module that every implementation team knows and every SharePoint or Drive migration ends up needing. If your organization has a link farm, this episode is for you.


First, a new widget: Page Reader


Our latest widget adds text-to-speech to any LumApps page. Drop it in, choose a voice, and hit play. It works on desktop and mobile, with different voice providers depending on the device.


The privacy angle matters here: everything runs locally in the browser. Your page content is never sent to a third-party service. That's also why mobile voice quality is a bit lower, but for anyone handling sensitive content, it's a fair trade. Find it in the ADC Partner space on the Hive.


Pro tip: bulk import links with the LumApps Toolbox


This one's an oldie but a goodie. The LumApps Toolbox is officially deprecated, but it still works, and it's still the fastest way to get hundreds of legacy links into LumApps.


Ivo walked through importing directory entries from a CSV. A few things that will save you time:


  • Site ID: Press Ctrl+Shift+? on any page to pull up the site instance properties.

  • Directory ID: This is the tricky one. It's not the content ID of the directory page. The easiest way to find it is to run an export first and pull the ID from the file.

  • Keep it minimal: You only need a few required columns. A label and a URL per entry is enough to get started.


Most of what the Toolbox used to handle, like bulk metadata updates, is now built into the All Content view. Importing directory entries is one of the few places where it still earns its keep.


How directory entries work


Think of it in three layers:


  • Central entries managed by admins or delegated roles

  • Personal entries and favorites that each user adds and manages themselves

  • Micro apps that live inside a directory alongside regular links


Directories are not the same as the user directory, which is a separate module. That mix-up comes up more often than you'd think.


Watch your permissions


You can delegate directory management through roles, but there's a catch. Anyone with that role can see every directory, not just the one they're responsible for. Give create and edit rights, not delete, unless you're confident the person knows what they're doing.


The hidden feature: custom fields


This was the highlight for Misha. Tucked away at the bottom of the directory module settings is a template option that lets you add custom fields to every entry. It was added quietly a few months ago, and most people haven't found it yet.


Field types include:


  • Links with custom labels

  • Email addresses

  • Phone numbers

  • Single or multiple selection lists (for example, project phase 1, 2, or 3)


Each field can be required or optional. In the demo, Misha added a support email and phone number to a Concur entry, so anyone searching for Concur sees exactly who to contact. Entries can also be limited to specific segments.


Two gotchas: click the checkbox to add each field before you hit OK, and save the page afterward. If you skip either step, your changes won't stick.


Bonus: entry descriptions are indexed by LumApps search, so a good description makes your links much easier to find.


Micro apps in your directory


Ivo showed how micro apps have become first-class citizens in LumApps. When you add a new entry, you can choose between a link and a micro app. His demo was a shift-swap app: pick a shift, pick a colleague, and swap, all without leaving the directory.


Users can favorite micro apps just like links, so you could build a single profile page that shows each person's favorite tools.


Directories also work on mobile. You can place them in streams, on the homepage, or inside Journeys.


Watch the replay here:

title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: LumApps’ Broadcasts Deep Dive
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: Misha and Ivo celebrate one year of ADC Live! by exploring LumApps Broadcasts. They cover how Broadcasts replaced legacy newsletters, build a personalized, segmented broadcast live, and share best practices for getting employees to open and engage. There's also a World Cup surprise.
lead: Misha and Ivo celebrate one year of ADC Live! by exploring LumApps Broadcasts. They cover how Broadcasts replaced legacy newsletters, build a personalized, segmented broadcast live, and share best practices for getting employees to open and engage. There's also a World Cup surprise.
html:
A year in


This episode marked one year of ADC Live!, about 27 episodes covering everything from architecture to AI to analytics. We didn't make a big fuss about it. We had a World Cup to talk about and a demo to run.


First, the World Cup


The tournament kicked off the next day, so we showed our new World Cup widget. Employees pick a match, predict the score, and can change their minds until kickoff. It works for any soccer match, so it doesn't expire when the final whistle blows. More at adc.dev.


Why Broadcasts


If you were around LumApps in 2017, you remember the newsletter module. It did the job, barely. Scheduling was clunky, layouts were rigid, and personalization was basically nonexistent.


Broadcasts replaced it. They live in LumApps' Content Strategy suite next to Campaigns (topic-based series like town halls or leadership updates) and Segments (audience targeting based on profile data). And they go well beyond email: push, SMS, Slack, Google Chat, and Teams are all on the table.


Watch the full replay below:




Can't find Broadcasts in your platform? It depends on your LumApps package. Ask your CSM.


The demo


A few things worth calling out:


  • The broadcast calendar shows everything sent, scheduled, and in draft in one monthly view. If you plan comms, you'll live here.

  • Banners, dividers, buttons, and two-column layouts take seconds to add.

  • We embedded a LumApps Play video from a past episode directly in the email.

  • One section, "New to ADC?", was restricted to a New Hires segment. Everyone gets the same broadcast, but only new hires see that block.

  • Send yourself a test, schedule it, or start from a template next time.

  • Pro tip: use their name


Broadcasts support personalization keywords, so your opener can greet each reader by first name, last name, or both. It's a small thing that makes a big difference in how people read the rest.


What makes people actually open them

  • Target carefully. Segment by role, relevance, or start date. If you want to reach people in their first 90 days, you can.

  • Don't flood inboxes. A steady campaign to the right people beats daily blasts to everyone.

  • Write better subject lines. If you're stuck, AI tools are surprisingly good at this.

  • Keep the look consistent, but vary the content. "Make your World Cup pick before kickoff" will get more clicks than another policy reminder.

  • Send when people are there. Login heat maps tell you when that is, even by location.

  • Have a plan. Keep a shared comms calendar with clear owners and approvals so messages don't collide.

title: LumApps Announces ADC’s enhanced Table of Contents Extensions in the May 2026 Release Notes
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: A new layout option brings greater flexibility to one of our LumApps extensions.
lead: A new layout option brings greater flexibility to one of our LumApps extensions.
html:
The ADC Advanced Table of Contents widget has received a significant enhancement: support for a horizontal layout mode. Previously available only in a vertical orientation, the widget can now be configured to display navigation items horizontally across the top of a page — offering a new and more versatile content navigation experience for LumApps administrators and page owners alike.

The update was notable enough to be featured directly in LumApps' own official release notes, reflecting the widget's standing as a trusted extension within the LumApps ecosystem.


What Changes With Horizontal Mode

The existing vertical mode organizes anchor-tag navigation items in a top-to-bottom list, well suited for sidebars and narrower column layouts. The new horizontal mode repositions those same navigation items across a single row, functioning more like a page-level navigation bar. This makes it particularly well suited for long-form content such as knowledge base articles, policy documents, product resource pages, and onboarding materials — anywhere a top-of-page navigation experience is more intuitive than a side panel.


All existing widget functionality carries over into the horizontal layout, including dynamic anchor-tag generation, smooth scrolling, sticky positioning, and the ability to copy and share direct links to specific sections of a page.


Why It Matters

For organizations managing large volumes of long-form content in LumApps, the horizontal mode expands the range of page designs and templates the widget can support. Content that previously required workarounds or alternative navigation approaches can now be addressed directly within the Table of Contents widget, without additional administrative overhead.

As with all ADC extension widgets, the configuration is managed at the template level — once set up, page owners can maintain their content independently without ongoing involvement from site administrators.


Learn more about this extension here

title: ADC Live! Presents: Release Notes Backstage
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: From AI-powered document scanning in workflows to long-awaited admin search — LumApp is making a bold shift to a platform that now touches your physical workspace too.
lead: From AI-powered document scanning in workflows to long-awaited admin search — LumApp is making a bold shift to a platform that now touches your physical workspace too.
html:
Here is a focused overview of the Release Notes portion of the session:

The session was built around a live, real-time walkthrough of the latest LumApps release notes — notable in itself, as the notes had been published just thirty minutes before the event went live. Rather than presenting pre-prepared commentary, the ADC team reviewed the release notes alongside the audience as they appeared, lending the session an immediate and practical character.

The release notes covered a broad range of updates spanning platform administration, content management, user directory infrastructure, and productivity. While several features addressed long-standing administrative pain points — particularly around search, notification management, and user provisioning — the more strategically significant updates centered on LumApps' expanding productivity and AI capabilities. The introduction of AI into LumApps workflows, highlighted as the first tangible output of the Beekeeper merger, was treated as a marker of a broader platform shift rather than an isolated feature release.

The ADC team was careful to contextualize the release notes not just as a list of updates, but as evidence of a clear directional change in how LumApps is positioning itself — moving from a content and communications platform toward a more comprehensive employee productivity environment. Several of the features covered were flagged for deeper exploration in future ADC Live! episodes, reflecting both the density of the release and the team's intent to give each capability the attention it warrants.

For organizations already operating on LumApps, the release was characterized as particularly actionable, with a number of updates available immediately and at least one item — the NGI user profile migration — carrying a firm deadline requiring administrator attention before the end of June.


Watch the replay

title: ADC Live! Presents: The LumApps-Beekeeper Value and a Beekeeper Deep Dive
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: Bridging the Gap: LumApps Content, Now in Beekeeper
lead: Bridging the Gap: LumApps Content, Now in Beekeeper
html:
Your frontline workers live on their phones. Your best company content lives in LumApps. Until now, those two worlds rarely met.


We developed a first-of-its-kind integration that brings LumApps content — starting with a dynamic, personalized org chart — directly into the Beekeeper mobile experience. No second login. No extra apps. Just the right information, in the right place, for every employee.


Watch the REPLAY ADC Live! event



How it works: Our proprietary identity translator seamlessly maps each user's Beekeeper profile to their LumApps identity in real time, so every employee sees content that's personalized to them — the moment they open Beekeeper.


What this means for your organization:

  • Reach your deskless workforce where they already are

  • Reuse the content and data you've already built in LumApps

  • Start small with one widget, then expand as you grow

  • Let ADC handle all the technical complexity — you focus on the rollout


From org charts to personalized training assignments, the possibilities for what you can surface in Beekeeper are virtually limitless. And as the LumApps and Beekeeper platforms continue to converge, organizations that get ahead of this integration now will be best positioned to take full advantage.

Ready to connect your digital workplace? 


Contact ADC to explore what your first Beekeeper widget could look like.

title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: LumApps Analytics & Platform Logs APIs w/ Amazing Ivo
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: Watch this replay of a deep dive with Amazing Ivo into LumApps' Analytics and Platform Log APIs
lead: Watch this replay of a deep dive with Amazing Ivo into LumApps' Analytics and Platform Log APIs
html:
LumApps provides a robust layer of analytics and platform logging that enables organizations to better understand and optimize their digital workplace. Through built-in analytics, companies can track user engagement, monitor content performance, and measure overall platform adoption. Metrics such as page views, interaction rates, and user activity trends help identify what content resonates most and where improvements are needed, allowing teams to make more informed, data-driven decisions around internal communications and user experience.


Complementing these insights, LumApps platform logs capture detailed records of user actions, system events, and administrative changes. These logs play a critical role in auditing and compliance by maintaining clear activity trails and enabling organizations to monitor behavior, troubleshoot issues, and ensure accountability. Event-level tracking—such as content updates, permission changes, and system interactions—provides a granular view of how the platform is being used across the organization.


All of this data becomes even more powerful through LumApps APIs, which allow organizations to extract analytics and log data for integration with external tools such as business intelligence platforms or data warehouses. This enables advanced reporting, real-time monitoring, and automated workflows tailored to specific organizational needs. Together, LumApps analytics and platform logs form a comprehensive data foundation that supports visibility, control, and continuous improvement across the digital workplace.


Watch the replay below:

title: Featuring the first LumApps-Beekeeper Extension by ADC - Organization Chart
author: Ariella Zubarev
excerpt: Just like in LumApps, this extensions displays the organization chart of a user who is signed in to Beekeeper, based on their defined organization level.
lead: Just like in LumApps, this extensions displays the organization chart of a user who is signed in to Beekeeper, based on their defined organization level.
html:
We're very excited to announce the first and the latest LumApps-Beekeeper Extension by ADC - Organization Chart


Just like in LumApps, this extension displays the organization chart of a user who is signed in to Beekeeper, based on their defined organization level. This innovative feature allows users to visualize their position within the broader organizational structure, providing a clear representation of how they fit into the company hierarchy. The organization chart not only showcases the individual’s immediate team members but also highlights the various departments and roles that are interconnected within the organization.


This functionality is particularly beneficial for new employees who are still getting acquainted with the company’s structure, as it helps them understand whom to approach for specific queries or collaborations. By providing a visual guide, the organization chart enhances communication and collaboration across different teams, fostering a more cohesive work environment. Additionally, it serves as a valuable tool for managers and team leaders, enabling them to identify gaps in their teams and recognize potential areas for development.


Moreover, the integration of the organization chart within Beekeeper ensures that users have easy access to this critical information directly within their workflow. This seamless integration minimizes the need to switch between multiple platforms, thereby streamlining the user experience. As employees navigate through their daily tasks, they can quickly reference the organization chart to clarify reporting lines or to discover new colleagues they may not have interacted with yet.


In summary, the LumApps-Beekeeper Organization Chart extension is a powerful addition that not only enhances visibility into the organizational structure but also promotes a culture of transparency and collaboration within the workplace. We are eager to see how this new feature will empower employees and contribute to a more informed and connected workforce.


To learn more about this extension, click here.

title: [REPLAY] ADC Live! Presents: Mobile Experience in LumApps
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: Let's look at some use cases for mobile and rreview some of the mobile configurations
lead: Let's look at some use cases for mobile and rreview some of the mobile configurations
html:
Overview of the ADC Live! Event

The ADC Live! event served as a comprehensive platform for participants to delve into the intricacies of configuring the mobile application, focusing on a variety of practical use cases that are essential for enhancing user engagement and functionality. Attendees were provided with in-depth insights and hands-on demonstrations that illuminated the process of tailoring the mobile app to meet specific organizational needs.

Use Cases Explored

Among the key use cases discussed during the event, one of the primary focuses was on **adding custom links and banners to surveys**. This feature allows organizations to create a more personalized experience for users by embedding links that direct them to relevant content or external resources. Banners can be strategically placed within surveys to attract attention, convey important messages, or promote new initiatives, thereby increasing participation rates and overall user interaction.

Content Management Enhancements

title: Space vs Community vs Content Type Pages?
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: Choosing the Right LumApps Content Structure: Spaces, Communities, and Content-Type Pages
lead: Choosing the Right LumApps Content Structure: Spaces, Communities, and Content-Type Pages
html:
SME ALERT: The following knowledge article is a deep dive into deep LumApps contents.


As you continue to evolve your LumApps employee experience platform, selecting the right area where to create your content is critical to delivering effective user experiences and streamlining content governance. LumApps offers three main options for content creation: Spaces, Communities, and Content-Type Pages; each offering unique strengths tailored to different organizational needs and use cases. Understanding the distinctions can help digital teams align structure with purpose, while optimizing scalability and engagement.


Spaces offer a simplified, out-of-the-box solution for teams or departments looking for a consistent and controlled environment. With a baked-in OOTB navigation experience consistent across all Space subpages (homepage, events, articles, etc.), Spaces ensure a cohesive user experience without the need for ongoing design maintenance. Their self-service nature, document storage capabilities, and governance controls make them ideal for teams that require autonomy without the complexity of custom development. Spaces also offer an Advanced Member role, allowing only special users rights to create Articles and Events.


Communities provide more design flexibility for teams. While they offer mostly similar governance features to Cpaces (minus the Advanced Member role), LumApps Communities allow greater customization on subpages such as posts and events pages. This makes them well-suited for teams who are more advanced in their design skills and wanting a more personalized touch.


Content-Type Pages, often used by internal communications or KM teams, deliver the highest level of control and editorial functionality. They include features like version history, content expiration, ghostwriting (publishing on behalf of executives), and detailed access controls. This is the highest level of structured content that LumApps has, and is best suited for formal / top-down communications, leadership announcement using ghostwriting features, or long, elaborate and rich KB / Wiki pages where rich editing and formatting capabilities, paired with advanced publication features, access and permissions are paramount.


Ultimately, choosing between these three options comes down to balancing governance, ease of use, and the level of user engagement required. While Spaces shine in simplicity and speed,


Communities support collaborative flexibility, and Content-Type Pages deliver structured, high-impact communication. Understanding these trade-offs will enable you to design and evolve the best and most sustainable portal to meet the diverse needs of your employee base.

title: Do you use AI to evaluate CVs?
author: Ivo Bellin Salarin
excerpt: A recent engineering effort highlights how building resilient, API-compatible data connectors and modular dbt transformations can unlock significant value in large-scale ETL pipelines, far beyond simple data movement.
lead: A recent engineering effort highlights how building resilient, API-compatible data connectors and modular dbt transformations can unlock significant value in large-scale ETL pipelines, far beyond simple data movement.
html:
Candidates selection for a position may feel like an overwhelming challenge (Oh! so many candidates applied at the same time!). So you may be tempted by using ChatGPT or other stuff to filter out candidates. (**Beware: this is not legal, at least not in the EU**). I am going to tell you why this is a bad idea!


- ChatGPT is cheesy. Back to the basics, it's a probabilistic text generator, so it will be influenced by the CV text. But their creators superimposed an optimistic take on life.

- ChatGPT is not sure 100%. It can spot a word in a CV (say: terraform) but if the candidate said "I used terraform for testing" openAI will count it as "experience acquired" (even if it's clearly a fake ;))

- ChatGPT doesn't add up like you do. Let's assume that the CV says 24 years of experience (but then you addition all the relevant experience items and get only 12).

- ChatGPT does not transfer that emotion that you experience when reading a CV. It's in your gut, and it's probably the best thing that you can extract from a CV.

- Certain trainings are worth mentioning on a CV, certain aren't. A human with experience knows the difference.

- Every candidate is different. If you were to compare them, you would probably missing elements that candidates did not highlight both. You get an idea about what the candidate is strong at reading the entirety of her/his CV.


What about the law? The EU AI Act classifies this task as high-risk. This implies a certain number of mitigation mechanisms that you should be putting in place to make sure that transparency, explainability and bias mitigation meet standards. Human supervision should be in place. And, you should be paying attention to where the candidate data is being sent (is this a publicly hosted service? Is this a self-hosted AI model?)


The GDPR then obliges you to 1) have a lawful basis (your business interest must outweigh the candidate privacy interest) 2) inform the candidate about how you are going to process their data, and 3) get a mandatory Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA).


I hope this helps make the right choice!

title: Reimagining ETL: Lessons from the Field
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: A recent engineering effort highlights how building resilient, API-compatible data connectors and modular dbt transformations can unlock significant value in large-scale ETL pipelines, far beyond simple data movement.
lead: A recent engineering effort highlights how building resilient, API-compatible data connectors and modular dbt transformations can unlock significant value in large-scale ETL pipelines, far beyond simple data movement.
html:
ETL is often seen as a solved problem—but at scale, and in the real world, it’s rarely straightforward. Recently, our team worked on a series of projects that reminded us how much value lies in crafting resilient, well-designed data pipelines that do more than just move data. We built and deployed multiple custom connectors designed to make external APIs compatible with Fivetran ingestions, among others.


These connectors didn’t just pass data through—they actively transformed the source format, managed state, handled pagination, dealt with API-specific quirks like error retrieval and rate limiting, and seamlessly interfaced with Fivetran’s expectations. Each connector was deployed as a stateless Cloud Run function, making them easy to scale and maintain.


In parallel, we designed a dbt-based transformation layer for a BigQuery dataset from a different data source. This let us modularize the logic, bring transparency to the data lineage, and align closely with the needs of downstream consumers—proof that dbt’s declarative model continues to be a force multiplier for data teams.

title: Partnership with The Glass Guru on the Looker to LumApps Integration
author: Misha Zubarev
excerpt: A look into one of our latest deep integrations between LumApps and Looker for The Glass Guru Franchise
lead: A look into one of our latest deep integrations between LumApps and Looker for The Glass Guru Franchise
html:
We believe in partnering with forward thinking organizations and technologies, and are very enthusiastic with our ongoing partnership with LumApps and with The Glass Guru Enterprises, Inc. on the Looker Integration project. 


Our latest integration between LumApps and Looker is for one of our valued customers, The Glass Guru. This integration creates a streamlined user experience in LumApps to view Looker dashboards without ever having to be authenticated in Looker itself; this equates to minimizing workplace disruption by saving users valuable time and frustrations having to login multiple times.


In the words of Sean Young, our key stakeholder for this project: 

“In the franchise realm, the impact of analytics cannot be overstated. By their nature, franchisees are eager to see how they stack up against their peers within the organization. Given the significance of this content, Guru HQ, our LumApps-powered Intranet, was the unequivocal choice for showcasing these analytics. The need for private, embedded analytics is why we chose Looker several years ago as our chosen analytics tool. Looker offers so much more than just analytics, but the software’s ability to feature embedded analytics anywhere was a significant feature for our brand.


As we’ve walked the path building out our data model(s), we finally reached the point where we were ready to streamline the usage of two great products; LumApps and Looker. We embarked on an integration journey with our long time partner and vendor Misha Zubarev of Ariella Digital Consulting.

This integration creates a streamed experience for our franchise users to view Looker dashboards directly within LumApps without a need to authenticate in Looker; this equates to minimizing workplace disruption by saving franchisees valuable time and frustrations having to figure out and deal with the frustrations of multiple login experiences. The integration also ensures we are utilizing Looker’s significant data governance features, ensuring our Lumapps users only have access to analytics built on datasets they are authorized to view.” 


Read more about why integrations are important for an Employee Experience Platform:


An Employee Experience platform aims to enhance the overall work environment and employee engagement by providing seamless and user-friendly tools for various HR processes, communication, collaboration, and learning. Integrating third-party applications within the EX platform brings numerous benefits that contribute to a comprehensive and effective experience for employees. Here's why third-party integrations are essential:


Consolidation and centralization. An EX platform often serves as a central hub for various HR functions. By integrating third-party applications that employees use regularly, such as project management tools, communication platforms, or productivity apps, the platform becomes a one-stop solution for employees' needs. This consolidation streamlines processes and reduces the need to switch between multiple applications, saving time and effort.


Enhanced functionality. While an EX platform may have a wide range of built-in features, there are specialized tools and services offered by third-party providers that might cater to specific needs or industries better. By integrating these external solutions, the EX platform can offer enhanced functionality, ensuring that employees have access to the best tools available in the market.


Customization and personalization. Each organization has unique workflows and preferences. Third-party integrations allow companies to customize the EX platform according to their specific requirements and tailor the experience to match their corporate culture. This customization fosters a sense of ownership and comfort among employees, leading to increased adoption and engagement.


Data synchronization and analytics. Third-party integrations enable seamless data synchronization between various applications. This integration ensures that employee data, such as performance metrics, learning progress, or feedback, is updated in real-time across the platform. It also allows for comprehensive data analytics, which can provide valuable insights into employee behavior, preferences, and areas of improvement.


Scalability and flexibility. As an organization grows or its needs evolve, it may adopt new tools or services to enhance operations. A flexible EX platform with the ability to integrate third-party applications makes it easier for companies to scale up and adapt to changing requirements without significant disruptions.


Employee empowerment and productivity. A well-integrated EX platform creates a user-friendly environment that empowers employees to perform their tasks efficiently. By accessing all necessary tools and information from a single platform, employees can focus on their work instead of dealing with the complexities of managing multiple applications.


Continuous improvement and innovation. Third-party integrations open the door to a vast ecosystem of innovative solutions. By partnering with external providers, an EX platform can stay up-to-date with the latest technological advancements and continuously improve its offerings to cater to the changing needs and preferences of employees.


In summary, third-party integrations play a vital role in an Employee Experience platform by expanding its capabilities, streamlining processes, and creating a cohesive and tailored experience for employees. This integration-driven approach enhances engagement, productivity, and overall job satisfaction, ultimately leading to a more positive and fulfilling work environment.
